newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- At least 10 people were killed when Army troopers pursued some 200 Moslem rebels who blocked a bridge in Maguindanao, then hijacked two passenger buses and took some 60 commuters hostage early yesterday morning. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- President Ramos said yesterday it is hard to resist the "widespread clamour" for him to run again in 1998. (STANDARD/TODAY/MALAYA)

- A secret deal entered into by the Philippine government will unfreeze the $500 million in Swiss deposits of the late strongman Ferdinand Marcos. This was disclosed yesterday by lawyers of 10,000 victims of human rights violations during the martial law regime who are claiming damages from the Marcos estate. (INQUIRER)
- Food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp yesterday undertook a virtual backdoor listing of its property arm by merging it with an inactive listed poultry subsidiary. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Philippine Central Bank yesterday assured the scheduled one percentage-point cut in reserve requirements on July 4 would not lead to inflationary pressures. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The country's automotive parts manufacturers are up in arms against a proposal by the Board of Investments to allow the importation of semi-knocked down units for new car models by local assemblers, saying it was the final straw that would kill the domestic car parts industry. (BULLETIN/STAR/MALAYA)
